title: Four of Wands Tarot Card Meaning: Upright, Reversed & Love
description: Four of Wands upright: celebration, homecoming, stability; reversed: tension at home. Love, work, advice and Waite's 1911 text. Ask your question.
h1: Four of Wands Tarot Card Meaning
image_alt: Four of Wands, 1909 Rider–Waite–Smith card: a garland hangs between four tall staves; two women raise bouquets before a castle wall and a red-roofed tower.
capsule: The Four of Wands stands for celebration, homecoming and stability, a joyful moment shared with your community. Reversed, it can show tension at home, a hollow celebration or a transition. A happy card, it asks you to enjoy what is good now. The reply is yes: the garland is already up, and people are coming out to celebrate.

blocks.heading: What is on the Four of Wands card?
paragraphs: Waite describes it this way: "From the four great staves planted in the foreground there is a great garland suspended; two female figures uplift nose-gays" (p. 190). Beside them, he adds, "is a bridge over a moat, leading to an old manorial house" (p. 190).

On the 1909 card the background is bright yellow, and the four tall staves with their garland of leaves and red-orange blossoms are the largest shapes in the frame; ribbons are tied to the two outer staves. The two women hold their flowers high, one in white and blue, the other in dark red. Behind them rises a gray wall with a tower under a pointed red roof. Small figures gather at the left, and a stone arch shows at the right.

blocks.heading: What did Waite write about the Four of Wands?
paragraphs: Waite says that here the meanings are "for once almost on the surface" (p. 190): what you see is what the card means. His list also includes "a species of domestic harvest-home" (p. 190), the old name for the feast at the end of the harvest.

Waite's reversed line is rare in the book: the meaning "remains unaltered", with prosperity and beauty still in place (p. 190). The modern reversed reading below is less sunny, and it is Arcana Diary's own.

blocks.heading: What does the Four of Wands mean upright?
paragraphs: Celebration comes first: a milestone, a gathering, a wedding or a party, any moment when people come together to mark something good. Homecoming is the second meaning: arriving where you are welcome, returning to people who feel like home, or making a place truly yours.
Under the garland there is also stability. The joy rests on a base that was built, so the card often follows finished work, a completed stage, a home or community settled enough to rest in.
What deserves to be marked in your life right now, and with whom would you share it?

blocks.heading: What does the Four of Wands mean reversed?
paragraphs: When the Four of Wands is reversed, it can show a hollow celebration, tension at home, or simply not feeling at home where you are. It also fits a transition: moving house, a change in family life, a group you are leaving or have not yet joined.
Sometimes the snag is waiting for everything to be perfect before enjoying it. A smaller, simpler celebration may be all that is needed.

blocks.heading: What does the Four of Wands mean in love?
paragraphs: Commitment and joy are the love themes: moving in, an engagement, a wedding, or a relationship that simply feels like home. In modern readings this is a classic card of happy milestones between partners.
Upside down, the card may describe a home atmosphere grown tense, a celebration that feels forced, or a passage between two stages of a relationship.
When there is no partner, it turns to belonging: friends, family and places where you are welcomed as you are, a warm base from which new connections grow easily.

blocks.heading: What does the Four of Wands mean for work and money?
paragraphs: A project reaching a milestone, a launch, a team that works well together, a party for finished work: this is the Four on the job. It favors workplaces that feel like a community.

For money, the card means stability and a secure base, often linked to home: a comfortable period, savings for a place of your own, spending on something shared and festive. Reversed, it can mean money strain during a change, such as the costs of a move, or tension about money at home.

blocks.heading: What is the advice of the Four of Wands?
paragraphs: Mark one good thing in your life on purpose: invite people over, put flowers in a corner of your space, raise a glass to a finished stage. Joy that is shared grows.

blocks.heading: Is the Four of Wands a yes or no card?
The Four of Wands as a person and as feelings
paragraphs: Read as someone you know, the Four of Wands is the host: warm and welcoming, the one who brings people together and makes any place feel like home. As feelings, it means happiness and a sense of security in a connection, the wish to celebrate it and to build a shared home or future. Reversed, the feeling is unsettled: the affection is there, but something about belonging or stability has not settled into place.

blocks.heading: The Four of Wands with other cards

pairs.text: Success that gets celebrated. Share the win with the people who helped.
A stable home and lasting family ties; roots worth a party.
Joy without reserve: a bright, open-hearted celebration.
Friction before the gathering. Settle small quarrels so everyone can relax.

blocks.heading: Four of Wands, Three of Cups or Ten of Cups?
paragraphs: The Three of Cups also celebrates, but Waite's picture is "Maidens in a garden-ground with cups uplifted" (p. 220), and today it is read as friendship and shared joy. The Ten of Cups shows, in Waite's words, an "Appearance of Cups in a rainbow" with "a home-scene beyond" (p. 206); its modern meaning is lasting emotional fulfillment. The Four of Wands marks the arrival itself: a milestone, a welcome, a base that now stands.

blocks.heading: Questions to ask yourself about the Four of Wands
paragraphs: What in my life deserves to be celebrated now?
Where do I truly feel at home?
Who would I like to share a good moment with?

faq.q: Is the Four of Wands a good or bad card?
faq.a: Good, one of the happiest cards of the Minor Arcana. It brings joy, belonging and a steady base. Reversed, it does not turn bad: it shows something unsettled at home or in a group that can be talked through. Waite even kept the reversed meaning bright (p. 190).

faq.q: Is the Four of Wands a wedding card?
faq.a: Often, yes: weddings, engagements and moving in together are among its typical modern meanings. Still, it describes a festive moment and a shared commitment, not a promise of a proposal. It can just as well be a family party, a housewarming or the end of a big project.

faq.q: Does the Four of Wands mean a new home?
faq.a: It can. A house to come back to and a settled place are central to the card, so a move, a housewarming or putting down roots often comes up. Waite's own list starts with country life and a "haven of refuge" (p. 190).

waite.quote: Country life, haven of refuge, … repose, concord, harmony, prosperity, peace … Reversed: The meaning remains unaltered; it is prosperity, increase, felicity, beauty, embellishment.
